title: Persona Attribute — Get — payload
description: Read one attribute the holder holds, by identifier. Values are withheld unless asked for, on the same two-step as persona/attribute/list: the expensive, disclosing path is the one a producer has to name.

attributeId.description: The attribute to read. One identifier, never a list: a maintainer that accepted several would recreate the enumeration this task exists to avoid.

includeValue.description: When false (the default), the attribute's metadata is returned and its `value` is not. The default is false even though a caller naming one attribute usually wants its value, because the alternative makes the disclosing path the one nobody has to ask for — and the audit row can then say whether plaintext left, which is the question worth being able to answer later.
includeValue.$comment: Mirrors includeValues on persona/attribute/list. The plural is a listing of many; this is one.

includeSensitive.description:
When false (the default), a request that asked for the value still does not receive it for an attribute resolving to `sensitivity: high` — the metadata is returned, the plaintext is not. Setting it asks for that too.

The second flag is not ceremony. A consumer that masks a value it has already received defends a screen; it does not keep a passport number out of a log, a crash dump, or a process's memory. The value never being sent is what does.

version.description:
Read a retained earlier version instead of the current one. Absent means current.

This is what makes "what did I show them in March" answerable: a disclosure record and a pinned profile entry both name a version, and without this a caller holding one has no way to read what it said. A version the holder has purged is `persona/attribute/get:versionPurged` — never a silent fall back to the current value, which would answer a question about the past with a fact about the present.

attribute.description: The attribute as at `version`, or as it stands when none was asked for. Its `value` is present only if the request asked for it and the attribute's sensitivity permitted it.

valueWithheld.description: True when the value was withheld although `includeValue` asked for it — the attribute resolves to `sensitivity: high` and `includeSensitive` was not set. Stated rather than left to inference: a consumer that reads an absent `value` as "this attribute has none" will show the holder an empty field where a passport number is, and conclude the record is broken.

retainedVersions.description:
The versions of this attribute the maintainer still holds, newest first, including the current one. Names versions and never their values.

It is here because a holder deciding whether to purge cannot see what purging would take away: which earlier versions exist, and therefore which pinned profile entries would stop presenting. A consumer that cannot enumerate them asks the holder to make an irreversible decision blind.
